construction: Each node with b children divides its inherited interval into b+1 equal local channels.
Channel 0 is retained by the parent-state; ordered child i receives channel i.
Therefore each child interval has width parent_width/(b+1), exactly matching the Local Emergence Law.
The node x-coordinate is the exact midpoint of its inherited interval.
Its token is encoded exactly as a rational base-12 offset inside its depth band.
Parent-child edges are part of the geometric object.

unification.meaning: the same locally derived quantity controls both influence and geometric scale

infinite_path_theorem_candidate.statement: Along any infinite descent path, every traversed node has at least one child, hence every interval contraction factor is <=1/2. Therefore interval width after k descents is <=2^-k and tends to zero.
infinite_path_theorem_candidate.consequence: Every infinite ordered descent determines a unique limiting geometric address x.

bounded_branching_mass_theorem.statement: If every node has at most B children, then total level mass satisfies M_{k+1} <= [B/(B+1)] M_k, so total mass <= B+1.
bounded_branching_mass_theorem.importance: An infinitely deep, infinitely populated hierarchy can still have finite canonical structural mass under bounded local branching.

caution: The geometry is canonical relative to the chosen Local Symmetry + Conservation axioms. If later axioms assign unequal local branch strengths, interval widths should be generalized proportionally.
